scene:
Three unlabelled areas read left to right, separated by generous space; do not number, title or name the areas.

LEFT AREA, the buyout: a single company building standing on one pedestal made of two stacked layers: the bottom layer is a large ochre block with a small bank building icon on its face (no word on it), labelled to its right €60M BORROWED; the top layer, directly under the building, is a thinner teal block with a few plain coins drawn on its face, labelled to its right €40M FUND MONEY. Beside the building, a small rising line with an upward arrow from a short bar to a taller bar, labelled EBITDA €10M → €15M.

MIDDLE AREA, one company, three sale prices: at the top an identical small copy of the same company building with a bracket beneath it, labelled SAME COMPANY. From the bracket three navy arrows lead down to three payout stacks of coins side by side, clearly different in height: a short stack labelled 7× → €65M, a medium stack labelled 10× → €110M, a tall stack labelled 12× → €140M.

RIGHT AREA, what engineering can claim: a simple bar chart (NOT a waterfall: every bar starts from the same baseline and none floats) of three separate vertical bars, left to right, with heights strictly in proportion 5 : 2 : 1: a tall teal bar labelled €50M EARNINGS; a bar less than half as tall, ochre, labelled €20M MULTIPLE; the shortest bar, half the height of the ochre one, with navy diagonal hatching and a small question mark inside, labelled €10M BOTH. Each label appears once, below its bar; the bars themselves contain no text or numbers. Below the bridge, an engineer with a notebook and a magnifying glass looking at a customer screen and a ruled ledger sheet (the ledger has only blank ruled lines, no heading or word), labelled EVIDENCE ALONG THE WAY.

All coins are plain discs with no symbols; draw no dollar, euro or other currency signs on any object. Buildings, documents, screens, ledgers and people carry no words, letters or numerals of their own. No chapter title, heading or book name anywhere.

TEXT: draw exactly these labels, each once and nothing else: €60M BORROWED, €40M FUND MONEY, EBITDA €10M → €15M, SAME COMPANY, 7× → €65M, 10× → €110M, 12× → €140M, €50M EARNINGS, €20M MULTIPLE, €10M BOTH, EVIDENCE ALONG THE WAY. Any other text is a defect.
alt: A company bought with €60 million borrowed and €40 million of fund money grows EBITDA from €10 million to €15 million; the same company sold at 7, 10 or 12 times EBITDA pays the fund €65 million, €110 million or €140 million; a bridge splits a gain into €50 million from earnings, €20 million from the multiple and €10 million from both, marked with a question mark, and an engineer gathers evidence along the way.
caption: One operating result, three investor outcomes, and why a sale gain cannot say how much engineering created.
